author: DTrim99
body:
That's a clean way to frame it, and it points at a real inconsistency on our side rather than a missing rebate.

PolicyEngine does book these prior-year-based rebates in the eligibility year. The **Rhode Island** child tax rebate — the direct analog, also $250/child (max 3) determined by the 2021 return and paid in fall 2022 — sits in Rhode Island's **2021** refundable-credit list, and New Mexico's 2021 income rebates are likewise modeled in **2021**. The **Connecticut** child tax rebate is the odd one out: it's in Connecticut's **2022** non-refundable-credit list, so PE books it against 2022 income tax and computes eligibility from 2022 income and dependents — even though eligibility is set by the 2021 return.

So the consistent fix is to move `ct_child_tax_rebate` to the 2021 eligibility year (as a refundable credit, the way Rhode Island's is handled). That drops it off the 2022 CT-1040, so PE's 2022 Connecticut income tax matches TaxAct at 2,094, and it lines up with your "apply to the year eligibility is determined" option. I've updated [PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9270](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/issues/9270) to reflect that. Thanks for the steer.
